capabilities: Upload pasted or dropped images to a GitHub repository
Insert a raw.githubusercontent.com embed link in place of the local file
Create a new public repository from the plugin settings
Generate and configure a fine-grained personal access token
Test push access and public visibility of the target repository
extras: README warns the target repository must be public (pasted images become publicly accessible) and the token is stored unencrypted in data.json, which should not be synced, committed, or shared.
motivation: The author notes that unlike Notion, Obsidian stores every pasted image as a local file, growing the vault.
problem: Obsidian saves every pasted image as a local file, so the vault keeps growing with screenshots and there is no built-in way to host them externally.

relations.evidence: Upload pasted (or dropped) images straight to your own GitHub repository

requires.name: Fine-grained personal access token with Contents read and write

summary: Uploads pasted or dropped images to your own GitHub repository and inserts the raw CDN link instead of saving the file locally.
